gen.title: Understanding Savings Growth and Key Terms

cards.stem: How is compound interest described when earnings build over time?
options: earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn
pay interest only on the original deposit amount
receive a one-time bonus with no later growth
cards.quote: Compound interest is when you earn interest on both the money you save and the interest you earn.
cards.hint: Focus on earning on both saved funds and prior earnings

cards.stem: What does the rate charged for borrowing represent?
options: A percentage of a sum borrowed that is charged by a lender or merchant
A flat monthly fee for keeping an account open
A grant that never requires repayment
cards.quote: Interest rate: A percentage of a sum borrowed that is charged by a lender or merchant for letting you use its money.
cards.hint: Think about a percentage tied to borrowing

cards.stem: How is schooling pursued beyond high school broadly defined?
options: Includes all forms of schooling after high school, not just college
Covers only four-year university enrollment
Refers solely to job training without classroom study
cards.quote: Post-secondary education: Includes all forms of schooling after high school, not just college.
cards.hint: Consider all options beyond high school, not only college

cards.stem: What characterizes an outlay made with an expected gain?
options: Something you spend your money on that you expect will earn a financial return
Money set aside that you plan never to use again
Cash kept at home with no expectation of growth
cards.quote: Investment: Something you spend your money on that you expect will earn a financial return.
cards.hint: Think about spending now to seek a later return
